headings.title: SMTO-BOOT-0015 — The model setup can't find a working NVIDIA graphics card

html:
SMTO-BOOT-0015 — The model setup can't find a working NVIDIA graphics card

GUID: 787daa7f-d976-4cf3-834d-d8c06324788f
Slug: boot-gpu-unavailable
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • Before installing or starting a model, SMTO checks that it can use the computer's NVIDIA graphics card (GPU). That check failed, so it stopped before installing anything or loading a model.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open a terminal and run nvidia-smi. It should show a table that lists your graphics card. If the command is missing or shows an error, install or repair the NVIDIA driver. The installer and the launcher both use nvidia-smi to find the card, and it only works when the NVIDIA driver works.
  2. If the driver install or repair asks for a restart, finish or stop any running work and models first, then restart the computer and run nvidia-smi again. A newly installed driver may not be active until the computer restarts, so the card can look missing until then.
  3. If this happened while starting a model, set PYTHON_BIN to the Python in the Conda environment where vLLM is installed (for example ~/miniforge3/envs/vllm/bin/python), then start the launcher again. The launcher checks the card through that Python, and a Python without graphics card support fails the check.
  4. If you run inside a container or WSL, make sure graphics card access is turned on for it. If CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is set, it must list card numbers that nvidia-smi shows. Containers and a wrong CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES value can hide the card even when the computer has one.

What success looks like

  • nvidia-smi lists your graphics card, and the installer moves on to Conda ("Using Conda" or "Installing Conda via Miniforge") or the launcher prints "CUDA preflight OK".

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0015 line and the Error reference line, plus the output of nvidia-smi, and send it to the person who manages this computer's graphics drivers. Don't turn off the launcher's graphics card check to get past this; the model can't run without a working card.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The vLLM installer could not run nvidia-smi or got no GPU names from it, or the Mythos launcher's nvidia-smi call or PyTorch CUDA preflight (torch import, torch.cuda.is_available, device_count) failed.

What this means

  • The installer cannot resolve nvidia-smi, its query fails or returns no GPU names; the Mythos launcher also emits this diagnostic if its PyTorch CUDA preflight fails, including import failure, unavailable CUDA or zero devices. The installer stops before creating a Conda environment, or the Mythos launcher stops in CUDA preflight before serving a model. This check alone cannot distinguish driver/library mismatch, GPU visibility restrictions, a PyTorch import problem or another probe failure.

Why this can happen

  • The installer cannot resolve nvidia-smi, its query fails or returns no GPU names; the Mythos launcher also emits this diagnostic if its PyTorch CUDA preflight fails, including import failure, unavailable CUDA or zero devices.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual nvidia-smi error, container/device permissions and driver/library consistency.

How to fix it

  • Confirm nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name --format=csv,noheader lists GPUs on the host or inside the container. For start-mythos-9b-unhinged.sh, run the preflight with the same interpreter (PYTHON_BIN, or ~/miniconda3/envs/vllm/bin/python when present) and check import torch, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.device_count() and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. Repair the driver or container GPU access; restart the host only if that driver repair requires it and active work is settled.
  • Check nvidia-smi where required, the selected Python/PyTorch environment, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and host/container GPU access. Complete a diagnosed driver repair before restarting the host, with active work settled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Restore the selected interpreter's CUDA access and the relevant NVIDIA probe; restart the host only if the diagnosed driver repair requires it and active work is settled.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected environment can discover the intended devices through the supported driver tools.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The installer stops before creating a Conda environment, or the Mythos launcher stops in CUDA preflight before serving a model.
  • This check alone cannot distinguish driver/library mismatch, GPU visibility restrictions, a PyTorch import problem or another probe failure.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
